$$P=3\,000\,000\times2^1.$$

A medicine in the bloodstream loses 20% of its concentration every hour.

Let $t$ be the time in hours. The amount remaining is $100(0.8)^t$ mg.

$$\begin{aligned}100(0.8)^t&<30\\(0.8)^t&<0.3\\t&>\log_{0.8}(0.3)\\t&>\frac{\log(0.3)}{\log(0.8)}\end{aligned}$$

The inequality reverses because $0<0.8<1$.

content.prompt:
A disease doubles the number of infected individuals every week.

If 50 people were infected at the start, after how long will 8 billion people be infected?

Give your answer in whole weeks and the nearest day.

answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the time in weeks.

$$\begin{aligned}50(2^t)&=8\,000\,000\,000\\2^t&=160\,000\,000\\t&=\log_2(160\,000\,000)\\t&\approx27.25349666.\end{aligned}$$

The remaining fraction of a week is $7\bigl(\log_2(160\,000\,000)-27\bigr)\approx1.7745$ days.

Therefore, the time is **27 weeks 2 days**, to the nearest day.

content.prompt: The temperature difference between a cup of coffee and its surroundings decreases by 25% every 5 minutes. After how long will it take for the temperature difference to be less than $5^\circ\mathrm{C}$? Answer to the nearest whole minute.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}60(0.75)^t&<5\\(0.75)^t&<\frac{1}{12}\\t&>\log_{0.75}\left(\frac{1}{12}\right)\end{aligned}$$
The inequality reverses because $0<0.75<1$.

The time in minutes satisfies
$$\begin{aligned}5t&>5\log_{0.75}\left(\frac{1}{12}\right)\\5t&>43.1884\ldots\end{aligned}$$
The temperature difference falls below $5^\circ\mathrm{C}$ after approximately 43 minutes, to the nearest whole minute.

inlines.text: When antibiotics are introduced into the human body, the concentration of the antibiotic in the bloodstream can be modelled by the equation

children.label: a

children.label: c
children.prompt: Solve for $x$, and hence show that it will take just over 2 hours to reach $2\,\mu\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$. Give times to 2 decimal places.

answer.short: $x=\frac13$ or $\frac23$. The two times are $5\ln\!\left(\frac32\right)\approx2.03$ hours and $5\ln3\approx5.49$ hours. The concentration first reaches $2\,\mu\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$ just over 2 hours after introduction.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}9x^2-9x+2&=0\\(3x-1)(3x-2)&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=\frac13$ or $x=\frac23$.

For $x=\frac23$:
$$\begin{align*}e^{-0.2t}&=\frac23\\-0.2t&=\ln\!\left(\frac23\right)\\t&=-\frac{\ln(2/3)}{0.2}\\t&\approx2.03\text{ hours}.\end{align*}$$
For $x=\frac13$:
$$\begin{align*}e^{-0.2t}&=\frac13\\-0.2t&=\ln\!\left(\frac13\right)\\t&=-\frac{\ln(1/3)}{0.2}\\t&\approx5.49\text{ hours}.\end{align*}$$
The first time is $2.03$ hours, which is just over 2 hours.

answer.short: The concentration rises as the antibiotic is absorbed, then falls as it is metabolised. It reaches the same concentration once while rising and once while falling.
answer.worked: Initially, absorption of the antibiotic causes its concentration in the bloodstream to rise. After reaching a peak, the concentration falls as the antibiotic is metabolised. It therefore reaches $2\,\mu\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$ once while rising and again while falling.

content.prompt: Solve:

answer.worked:
Let $u=\sin x$.
$$\begin{align*}6u^2+7u-5&=0\\(2u-1)(3u+5)&=0\\u&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad u=-\frac53.\end{align*}$$
Since $-1\leq\sin x\leq1$, only $\sin x=\frac12$ is valid.
For $x\in[0,2\pi]$:
$$x=\frac{\pi}{6}\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{5\pi}{6}.$$

Let $y=\log_3x$, where $x>0$.
$$\begin{align*}6y^2+7y-5&=0\\(2y-1)(3y+5)&=0\\y&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad y=-\frac53.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\log_3x&=\frac12\\x&=3^{1/2}=\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
Or
$$\begin{align*}\log_3x&=-\frac53\\x&=3^{-5/3}\\x&=\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{3^5}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{243}}.\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy $x>0$.

Let $z=e^x$.
$$\begin{align*}6z^2+7z-5&=0\\(2z-1)(3z+5)&=0\\z&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad z=-\frac53.\end{align*}$$
Since $e^x>0$, only $e^x=\frac12$ is valid.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\ln\left(\frac12\right)\\x&=-\ln2.\end{align*}$$

• For the natural logarithm, always write either \(\ln x\) or \(\log_e x\)
